content:
Apple launched the latest Mac mini and Mac Studio models today. Alongside the product announcements, several Magic Keyboard accessories in its lineup have also received minor updates.

The newest Magic Keyboard removes the text labels on keys, replacing them with icons instead.

Apple's Mac mini and Mac Studio come with more powerful upgrades, including next-generation M6 chips and the high-end M5 Ultra, among other new processors.

The latest models are available for pre-order now: order the Mac mini here, and the Mac Studio here.

Beyond the desktop computer improvements, Apple has also updated the Magic Keyboard lineup, with the new versions featuring a subtle change.

The latest Magic Keyboard removes the text labels on many keys, replacing them with icons instead.

Apple previously made the same change on the MacBook Neo, MacBook Air, and MacBook Pro, and now the Magic Keyboard has received the same update.

Here are the changes across all the new Magic Keyboard models:

  • Magic Keyboard: US$99
  • Magic Keyboard with Touch ID: US$149
  • Magic Keyboard with Touch ID and Numeric Keypad: US$179

Frequently used keys such as Tab, Caps Lock, Return, Shift, and Delete no longer display text, showing only icons instead. On the extended models with a numeric keypad, keys like Home, Page Up, and Page Down have also been replaced with brand-new icons in place of text.

Popular comment from Caesarrr

I really don't understand this approach. You know it adds friction for users—what benefit is worth sacrificing the user experience?

Apart from switching to icons, the new Magic Keyboard looks almost identical to the previous model. All versions support USB-C, with the same features and layout as before.

If you'd like to order the new Magic Keyboard through Amazon rather than Apple, you can purchase them here: Magic Keyboard, version with Touch ID, and version with Touch ID and Numeric Keypad (in black).

What are your thoughts on the change to remove text labels from the keys? Let us know in the comments.
